text.p: U.S. credit rating agency Moody's Investors Service on Monday confirmed the credit ratings of Swedish commercial bank Svenska Handelsbanken and of mortgage bank Stadshypotek.
Handelsbanken last Thursday announced a 22.9 billion crown takeover bid for Stadshypotek, which is Sweden's largest mortgage lender with a third of the market.
Moody's confirmed Handelsbanken's ratings of Aa3 long-term deposit rating, A1 subordinated debt rating, Prime-1 short term deposit rating and B financial strength rating.

It said the proposed cash takeover would enable Handelsbanken to attain a commanding position in Sweden's mortgage market and stengthen considerably its standing at the forefront of the country's banking sector.

"This rating action reflects Moody's belief that this potential acquisition ... will enhance its franchise value and will lower the overall risk of the resulting group, without materially hurting Handelsbanken's strong recurring earning power," the credit rating agency said in a statement.

Moody's said this would more than offset in the long run the significant drop in Handelsbanken's core capitalisation following the acquisition, especially since the restoration of stronger capital ratios can be expected in the years to come.
Moody's also confirmed Stadshypotek's A2/Prime 1 ratings.
"Its acquisition by Handelsbanken if it occurred would create longer term benefits in the terms of additional revenue generation and better cost efficiency," the agency said.
"The likelihood of such trends create positive ramifications for Stadshyptoek's long-term debt ratings."

Moody's said if the take-over went ahead, it expected the group to focus on managing the integration process of Stadshypotek and on strengthening the earning power of its domestic franchise and its core capitalisation.
